name: The Peel Runs (Condemned Building Freerun Circuit)
description: An unsanctioned freerunning circuit that takes place exclusively inside condemned or scheduled-demolition structures in Tiers 1 through 3 — the 'Peel' referring to both the peeling ferrocrete of the buildings and the act of stripping a route down to its essential danger. Unlike the Strata Runs, the Peel Runs have no fixed course: routes are scouted and announced 90 minutes before the event, forcing runners to adapt in real time to unknown architecture. Both augmented and natural-body runners compete together with no division, though aug-heavy runners are informally penalized in community scoring for 'buying the gap.' The circuit's most famous venue, the Halvorsen-Ngozi Tower in Tier 2's condemned Westlake block, hosted eleven consecutive Peel events before its demolition in 2221 — the final run was held during the demolition itself.
cultural_impact: The Peel Runs have created a cross-tier subculture of runners who reject the corporate-sponsored cleanliness of sanctioned leagues, and the 90-minute announcement window has spawned a secondary culture of obsessive urban geography nerds who spend their weeks pre-scouting condemned buildings to have an edge. Several runners have died, which has paradoxically increased participation.
key_figures: Tomás Achebe-Lindqvist (founding runner, three-time circuit champion)
Yuki Osei-Petrov (route scout and announcer, known as 'the Cartographer')
Daria Mwangi-Svensson (aug-runner who sparked the 'buying the gap' debate)
locations: The Accordion Block, the Gray Zone district 4 (current primary venue)
Yuki's Scouting Den, Tier 2 transit underpass
story_hooks: The 90-minute announcement for a Peel Run leads to a building that is not condemned — it is fully occupied, and someone has forged the demolition paperwork to lure the runners inside.
Tomás Achebe-Lindqvist vanishes during a solo scout of a new venue and is found three days later with no memory of the intervening time and chrome he did not have before.
A Tier 4 corponation approaches Yuki the Cartographer with an offer to sanction the Peel Runs — turning them into a branded event — and the community fractures violently over the offer.
